title: Lost Comms: AVEF & MEA

faa.title: IFR operations: Two-way radio communications failure

hook: The radio just died in the clouds. What now?

scenes.narration: Level at eight thousand, solid I M C over the ridge line. Center hands you off — and the new frequency is dead silence. So is the old one. Kid... it's just you and ninety-one one eighty-five now.
Center never gave you a new route. You have your last assigned one, and what you filed. Which do you fly? Commit.
You fly what you were ASSIGNED. The order is A V E F: Assigned. Being vectored? Direct to what the Vector was for. Then Expected. Filed comes last.

Altitude — highest of three, per segment: the M E A, what ATC told you to Expect, what you were Assigned. Why highest? ATC protects the block where they last knew you'd be, and the rocks own everything below the M E A.
And if you break out into V F R? Stay V F R and land. A handheld radio is two hundred bucks — the cheapest life insurance on the market.
Eyes off the screen. The route order, and the three altitudes you pick the highest of. Out loud.
Route: Assigned, Vectored, Expected, Filed. Altitude: highest of M E A, Expected, Assigned. And keep flying the airplane — it doesn't know the radio's dead.
onScreenText: Alt: highest of MEA / E / A

scenes.narration: From the holding lesson — the narrow seventy-degree sliver. Which entry lives there?
Ninety-one one eighty-five. Two paragraphs. Memorize both.

quiz.question: Lost comms in IMC with no new route received. Under 91.185 you fly:
choices: The route last assigned by ATC
quiz.explanation: AVEF: Assigned first; if being Vectored, direct to the fix/route the vector was for; then Expected; then Filed.

quiz.question: Lost comms altitude for each segment is the HIGHEST of:
quiz.explanation: 91.185(c)(2): fly the highest of the minimum IFR altitude (MEA), the altitude ATC told you to expect, or your last assigned altitude.

quiz.question: Radio fails and you encounter VFR conditions. You should:
choices: Continue VFR and land as soon as practicable
Climb back into IMC and fly AVEF
quiz.explanation: 91.185(b): if you hit VFR conditions after the failure, remain VFR and land as soon as practicable.
